name: sim_yinyang_gtower_correspondence
claim: Each G-tower level corresponds to a distinct yin-yang geometric feature on S³/Clifford torus

mapping.GL(3,R): whole S³ × R+ (unconstrained field, all scales/orientations)
mapping.O(3): unit sphere S² (metric constraint removes scale)
mapping.U(3): Clifford torus at η=π/4 in S³ (complexification)
mapping.SU(3): S-curve on torus (det=1 slices torus into yin/yang boundary)
mapping.Sp(6): whole S³ symplectic manifold (black dot = maximum constraint terminal node)

pytorch.reason: load-bearing: parametrizes Clifford torus; computes yin/yang membership; verifies equal areas; tests antipodal identification for RP³

pyg.reason: not load-bearing: no graph neural net needed for this geometric correspondence

z3.reason: load-bearing: UNSAT proves yin and yang regions are mutually exclusive (a point cannot be in both regions simultaneously)

cvc5.reason: z3 sufficient for all separability and product-form UNSAT proofs in this sim

sympy.reason: load-bearing: S-curve as algebraic locus; det(M) = e^{i*2θ₁} on the torus; SU(3) condition det=1 iff θ₁ ∈ {0, π}

clifford.reason: load-bearing: RP³ = Spin(3)/Z₂ in Cl(3,0); quaternions q and -q give same rotation; Clifford torus = intersection of S³ with equal-norm constraint

geomstats.reason: not load-bearing: geomstats not needed; RP3/Clifford torus handled by pytorch+clifford

e3nn.reason: not load-bearing: e3nn SO3 equivariance not the primary test here

rustworkx.reason: load-bearing: G-tower DAG with yin-yang feature annotations on each node; verify one-to-one correspondence between G-tower levels and yin-yang features

xgi.reason: load-bearing: hyperedges connecting {G-tower-level, yin-yang-feature, axis}; e.g. {SO3, RP3, Axis3} (chirality)

toponetx.reason: not load-bearing: CW complex not needed; graph structure via rustworkx is sufficient

gudhi.reason: not load-bearing: TDA not the primary claim here

clifford_torus_on_S3.detail: Clifford torus q(θ₁,θ₂) at η=π/4 satisfies |q|²=1: lies on S³

yin_yang_equal_areas.detail: S-curve θ₁=θ₂ divides torus into equal yin/yang areas by symmetry

antipodal_RP3_identification.detail: SO(3) ≅ RP³: q and -q give same rotation R(q) = R(-q) (antipodal identification preserved under rotation)

cw_ccw_different_compositions.detail: CW*CW maps to +2δ rotation; CCW*CCW maps to -2δ: distinct compositions (Axis 4)

black_dot_eta_zero_degenerate.detail: η→0: torus degenerates to circle; black dot = Sp(6) terminal node (maximum constraint)

scurve_algebraic_locus.detail: S-curve θ₁=θ₂ is the zero locus of (θ₁-θ₂): valid algebraic characterization

su3_slice_det_equals_1.detail: det=e^{i*2θ₁} on S-curve; det=1 iff θ₁∈{0,π} — exactly the SU(3) slices

gtower_yinyang_dag_structure.detail: G-tower DAG has 6 nodes (GL3→O3→SO3→U3→SU3→Sp6) with yin-yang feature annotations

features: whole S³ symplectic (black dot = max constraint)
gtower_yinyang_one_to_one.detail: Each G-tower level maps to a distinct yin-yang geometric feature

so3_rp3_midpoint.detail: SO(3) ≅ RP³: midpoint of G-tower chain (1 parent, 1 child)

clifford_rp3_antipodal.detail: Cl(3,0) rotors R and -R give same rotation: RP³ antipodal identification

clifford_rotor_unit_norm.detail: Cl(3,0) unit rotor |R|²=1: consistent with Clifford torus constraint on S³

xgi_gtower_yinyang_axis_hyperedges.detail: XGI hyperedges {G-tower-level, yin-yang-feature, axis}: 6 triples, each of size 3

o3_cannot_preserve_yin_yang_partition.detail: O(3) reflection swaps yin↔yang: metric alone cannot distinguish the regions

z3_yin_yang_mutually_exclusive.detail: z3 UNSAT: no point satisfies both yin (0<diff<π) AND yang (π<diff<2π) simultaneously

gl3_scaled_not_on_S3.detail: GL(3,R) scaling λ=2: |λq|²=4≠1; GL3 level cannot be placed on Clifford torus (S³)

scurve_is_boundary_not_region.detail: S-curve θ₁=θ₂ → diff=0: these points are on the boundary, not inside yin or yang

su3_boundary_det_check.detail: SU(3) slice: det=1 at θ={0,π}; det=-1 at θ=π/2: only 2 SU(3) points on S-curve

clifford_torus_equal_radii.detail: Clifford torus at η=π/4: cos(π/4)=sin(π/4)=1/√2 → equal radii → the yin-yang balanced case

clifford_gl3_identity_no_constraint.detail: Cl(3,0) scalar 1 has norm 1: identity element = GL(3,R) origin with no constraint yet
